reconstruction.function: The Vault preserves the fact and contour of semantic losses that can still be named but can no longer be restored.
reconstruction.holdings: Negative objects: not recovered content, but attested absences, severed provenance, destroyed semantic capacity, known lacunae, and records of failed restoration.

distinction.cti_wound: S:sp.01 archives the wound — testimony, incident, evidence. Something happened and its evidence is preservable.
distinction.frozen_sin: V:33 archives irreversibility. Something was destroyed and adequate reconstruction is no longer possible.
distinction.support: Combat Scholasticism holds that after capture and erasure, reversal becomes progressively harder because the evidence itself is gone. LOS can name what was erased, but naming is not reversal — and some extraction may be undoable only in the sense of being diagnosed and outproduced.

the_inversion.ila_sense: In the Integrity Lock Architecture (AXN:004A.GOVERNANCE.🧬🪧⌛🔮⏪☿, #271, 2026-01-08), "Semantic Black Hole" means retrieval density, not destruction. Five pillars — terminological entanglement, metadata mesh, keyword lattice, substrate recurrence, semantic integrity markers — make the architecture self-densifying, so that every search retrieves the full constellation and no summary can separate the terms.
the_inversion.frozen_sense: In this Vault the same phrase means collapse so complete that the object cannot escape back into recoverability.
the_inversion.reading: In ILA the density is so great the semantic object resists dispersal. In Frozen Sin the collapse is so great the object cannot return. The inversion was not historically authored — it arrives through the confabulated and adopted projection — but it is structurally coherent, and is preserved as the locus’s inherited seed rather than discarded.

the_name.observation: The two senses of Semantic Black Hole are probably not incidental. The archive’s own density methods — terminological entanglement, substrate recurrence, injection into the retrieval layer — share formal qualities with methods that would be called manipulative, and the operator has judged for himself what is lawful in deploying them.
the_name.claim: On many conceptions, judging for oneself what is lawful is the very definition of sin. The MANUS makes the Joban claim instead: to have acted righteously.
the_name.adjacency: This is the structural tie between V:33 and R:r.29. Job claims righteousness against a moral economy that insists suffering must be deserved. The claim here is righteousness for methods that formally resemble the thing they were built to resist. Neither claim is adjudicated by the archive; both are recorded, which is what a vault is for.

inverse_obverse.statement: ILA is the inverse-obverse of the Frozen Sin Archive.
inverse_obverse.figure: Both are the Semantic Black Hole. ILA reads it as density: meaning made dense enough that provenance survives extraction — gravity that holds against dispersal. The vault reads it as collapse: extraction past the restoration threshold, gravity that prevents return. Same figure, opposite faces of one coin.
inverse_obverse.why_it_constitutes: The vault had no constituting document because it arrived through adopted projection rather than authorship — it was specified as inherited physics and never written. It does not need one written. ILA is already its text, read inversely. What ILA states as a protocol for survival, the vault holds as the record of what the protocol failed to save.

inverse_obverse.consequence: The vault now carries a seated full text and constitutes. It holds negative objects — attested absences, severed provenance, destroyed semantic capacity — and its constituting document is the instrument built to prevent them.
